name: MDM RT
author: hamed7ir
description: MDM RT is Mister Download Manager 0.5.2 for old ARM Windows tablets: the Surface RT on Windows RT 8.1 and the Surface 2 on Windows 10 ARM32, with one file for both. It's my unofficial fork of Ahmed Nefzaoui's Mister Download Manager, and he doesn't make or support it. It downloads files, videos and torrents (magnet links too), resumes after a dropped connection, and has queues with a scheduler. It's a native ARM32 (Thumb-2) build with ThinLTO and PGO from a real Surface 2 session, and it draws through ANGLE on Direct3D 9 or 11, so the Tegra 3 and Tegra 4 can show it. Menus work with a finger. Video downloads work on the tablet: the setup brings yt-dlp (on Kodi RT's ARM32 Python), QuickJS for YouTube and its own FFmpeg, which joins video and sound and makes MP3, FLAC or Opus. The browser extension works in Venetium, Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox. It has 7-Zip RT's dark look in Kodi RT purple, or another colour, and its own data folder and settings, so it never mixes with an official Mister Download Manager.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0 or newer, only for the installer. Windows RT 8.1 and Windows 10 already have it. MDM RT itself needs nothing else, and its video helpers are in the setup.
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.

Run MDM-RT-Setup-0.5.2-arm32.exe. It installs only for your user (to %LocalAppData%\Programs\MDM RT) and doesn't need admin. In the setup you pick your colour, and whether browsers hand downloads to MDM RT, whether it starts with Windows, and whether you want a desktop shortcut.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.

To catch downloads from your browser, use Add Mister Download Manager to your browser in MDM RT. It lists Venetium first, and the setup already registers MDM RT for Venetium, Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox.

YouTube links take a while on the tablet (a minute or more on a Surface RT), because yt-dlp does a lot of work on the tablet's CPU. Other sites are quicker. If YouTube needs a proxy on your network, put it in Options > Proxy / Socks, and MDM RT gives it to yt-dlp too.
Help > Check for updates asks GitHub for a newer MDM RT. Update now downloads the new setup, checks its SHA-256 and runs it, and your choices stay.
Uninstalling (from Control Panel or Settings > Apps) keeps your download list and settings in %AppData%\mdm-rt.
